units.leftText: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are in the Dispersion: Greetings.
units.rightText: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are of the Dispersion, greeting.

units.leftText: Count it all joy, my brothers, when you fall into various temptations,
units.rightText: Count it all joy, my brethren, when ye fall into manifold temptations;
leftNotes: 1:2 The word for “brothers” here and where context allows may also be correctly translated “brothers and sisters” or “siblings.”

units.leftText: knowing that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
units.rightText: knowing that the proving of your faith worketh patience.

units.leftText: Let endurance have its perfect work, that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
units.rightText: And let patience have its perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, lacking in nothing.

units.leftText: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
units.rightText: But if any of you lacketh wisdom, let him ask of God, who giveth to all liberally and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

units.leftText: But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed.
units.rightText: But let him ask in faith, nothing doubting: for he that doubteth is like the surge of the sea driven by the wind and tossed.

units.leftText: For that man shouldn’t think that he will receive anything from the Lord.
units.rightText: For let not that man think that he shall receive anything of the Lord;

units.leftText: He is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
units.rightText: a doubleminded man, unstable in all his ways.

units.leftText: Let the brother in humble circumstances glory in his high position;
units.rightText: But let the brother of low degree glory in his high estate:

units.leftText: and the rich, in that he is made humble, because like the flower in the grass, he will pass away.
units.rightText: and the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.

units.leftText: For the sun arises with the scorching wind and withers the grass; and the flower in it falls, and the beauty of its appearance perishes. So the rich man will also fade away in his pursuits.
units.rightText: For the sun ariseth with the scorching wind, and withereth the grass; and the flower thereof falleth, and the grace of the fashion of it perisheth: so also shall the rich man fade away in his goings.

units.leftText: Blessed is a person who endures temptation, for when he has been approved, he will receive the crown of life which the Lord promised to those who love him.
units.rightText: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation; for when he hath been approved, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord promised to them that love him.

units.leftText: Let no man say when he is tempted, “I am tempted by God,” for God can’t be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
units.rightText: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God; for God cannot be tempted with evil, and he himself tempteth no man:

units.leftText: But each one is tempted when he is drawn away by his own lust and enticed.
units.rightText: but each man is tempted, when he is drawn away by his own lust, and enticed.

units.leftText: Then the lust, when it has conceived, bears sin. The sin, when it is full grown, produces death.
units.rightText: Then the lust, when it hath conceived, beareth sin: and the sin, when it is fullgrown, bringeth forth death.

units.leftText: Don’t be deceived, my beloved brothers.
units.rightText: Be not deceived, my beloved brethren.

units.leftText: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation nor turning shadow.
units.rightText: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation, neither shadow that is cast by turning.

units.leftText: Of his own will he gave birth to us by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.
units.rightText: Of his own will he brought us forth by the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.

units.leftText: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
units.rightText: Ye know this, my beloved brethren. But let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

units.leftText: for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
units.rightText: for the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

units.leftText: Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
units.rightText: Wherefore putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.

units.leftText: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
units.rightText: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deluding your own selves.

units.leftText: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror;
units.rightText: For if any one is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a mirror:

units.leftText: for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.
units.rightText: for he beholdeth himself, and goeth away, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.

units.leftText: But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues, not being a hearer who forgets but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he does.
units.rightText: But he that looketh into the perfect law, the law of liberty, and so continueth, being not a hearer that forgetteth but a doer that worketh, this man shall be blessed in his doing.

units.leftText: If anyone among you thinks himself to be religious while he doesn’t bridle his tongue, but deceives his heart, this man’s religion is worthless.
units.rightText: If any man thinketh himself to be religious, while he bridleth not his tongue but deceiveth his heart, this man’s religion is vain.

units.leftText: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
units.rightText: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this, to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unspotted from the world.

units.leftText: My brothers, don’t hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.
units.rightText: My brethren, hold not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.

units.leftText: For if a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, comes into your synagogue, and a poor man in filthy clothing also comes in,
units.rightText: For if there come into your synagogue a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, and there come in also a poor man in vile clothing;

units.leftText: and you pay special attention to him who wears the fine clothing and say, “Sit here in a good place;” and you tell the poor man, “Stand there,” or “Sit by my footstool”
units.rightText: and ye have regard to him that weareth the fine clothing, and say, Sit thou here in a good place; and ye say to the poor man, Stand thou there, or sit under my footstool;

units.leftText: haven’t you shown partiality among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?
units.rightText: do ye not make distinctions among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?

units.leftText: Listen, my beloved brothers. Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom which he promised to those who love him?
units.rightText: Hearken, my beloved brethren; did not God choose them that are poor as to the world to be rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he promised to them that love him?

units.leftText: But you have dishonored the poor man. Don’t the rich oppress you and personally drag you before the courts?
units.rightText: But ye have dishonored the poor man. Do not the rich oppress you, and themselves drag you before the judgment-seats?

units.leftText: Don’t they blaspheme the honorable name by which you are called?
units.rightText: Do not they blaspheme the honorable name by which ye are called?

units.leftText: However, if you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.
units.rightText: Howbeit if ye fulfil the royal law, according to the scripture, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself, ye do well:

units.leftText: But if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.
units.rightText: but if ye have respect of persons, ye commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

units.leftText: For whoever keeps the whole law, and yet stumbles in one point, he has become guilty of all.
units.rightText: For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet stumble in one point, he is become guilty of all.

units.leftText: For he who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not commit murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.
units.rightText: For he that said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not kill. Now if thou dost not commit adultery, but killest, thou art become a transgressor of the law.

units.leftText: So speak and so do as men who are to be judged by the law of freedom.
units.rightText: So speak ye, and so do, as men that are to be judged by a law of liberty.

units.leftText: For judgment is without mercy to him who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
units.rightText: For judgment is without mercy to him that hath showed no mercy: mercy glorieth against judgment.

units.leftText: What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can faith save him?
units.rightText: What doth it profit, my brethren, if a man say he hath faith, but have not works? can that faith save him?

units.leftText: And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food,
units.rightText: If a brother or sister be naked and in lack of daily food,

units.leftText: and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it?
units.rightText: and one of you say unto them, Go in peace, be ye warmed and filled; and yet ye give them not the things needful to the body; what doth it profit?

units.leftText: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.
units.rightText: Even so faith, if it have not works, is dead in itself.

units.leftText: Yes, a man will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by my works.
units.rightText: Yea, a man will say, Thou hast faith, and I have works: show me thy faith apart from thy works, and I by my works will show thee my faith.

units.leftText: You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe—and shudder.
units.rightText: Thou believest that God is one; thou doest well: the demons also believe, and shudder.

units.leftText: But do you want to know, vain man, that faith apart from works is dead?
units.rightText: But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith apart from works is barren?

units.leftText: Wasn’t Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?
units.rightText: Was not Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son upon the altar?

units.leftText: You see that faith worked with his works, and by works faith was perfected.
units.rightText: Thou seest that faith wrought with his works, and by works was faith made perfect;

units.leftText: So the Scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him as righteousness,” and he was called the friend of God.
units.rightText: and the scripture was fulfilled which saith, And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned unto him for righteousness; and he was called the friend of God.

units.leftText: You see then that by works a man is justified, and not only by faith.
units.rightText: Ye see that by works a man is justified, and not only by faith.

units.leftText: In the same way, wasn’t Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way?
units.rightText: And in like manner was not also Rahab the harlot justified by works, in that she received the messengers, and sent them out another way?

units.leftText: For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, even so faith apart from works is dead.
units.rightText: For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, even so faith apart from works is dead.

units.leftText: Let not many of you be teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive heavier judgment.
units.rightText: Be not many of you teachers, my brethren, knowing that we shall receive heavier judgment.

units.leftText: For we all stumble in many things. Anyone who doesn’t stumble in word is a perfect person, able to bridle the whole body also.
units.rightText: For in many things we all stumble. If any stumbleth not in word, the same is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body also.

units.leftText: Indeed, we put bits into the horses’ mouths so that they may obey us, and we guide their whole body.
units.rightText: Now if we put the horses’ bridles into their mouths that they may obey us, we turn about their whole body also.

units.leftText: Behold, the ships also, though they are so big and are driven by fierce winds, are yet guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires.
units.rightText: Behold, the ships also, though they are so great and are driven by rough winds, are yet turned about by a very small rudder, whither the impulse of the steersman willeth.
leftNotes: 3:4 “Behold”, from “ἰδοὺ”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: So the tongue is also a little member, and boasts great things. See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!
units.rightText: So the tongue also is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how much wood is kindled by how small a fire!

units.leftText: And the tongue is a fire. The world of iniquity among our members is the tongue, which defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature, and is set on fire by Gehenna.
units.rightText: And the tongue is a fire: the world of iniquity among our members is the tongue, which defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the wheel of nature, and is set on fire by hell.

units.leftText: For every kind of animal, bird, creeping thing, and sea creature is tamed, and has been tamed by mankind;
units.rightText: For every kind of beasts and birds, of creeping things and things in the sea, is tamed, and hath been tamed by mankind:

units.leftText: but nobody can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
units.rightText: but the tongue can no man tame; it is a restless evil, it is full of deadly poison.

units.leftText: With it we bless our God and Father, and with it we curse men who are made in the image of God.
units.rightText: Therewith bless we the Lord and Father; and therewith curse we men, who are made after the likeness of God:

units.leftText: Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so.
units.rightText: out of the same mouth cometh forth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.

units.leftText: Does a spring send out from the same opening fresh and bitter water?
units.rightText: Doth the fountain send forth from the same opening sweet water and bitter?

units.leftText: Can a fig tree, my brothers, yield olives, or a vine figs? Thus no spring yields both salt water and fresh water.
units.rightText: can a fig tree, my brethren, yield olives, or a vine figs? neither can salt water yield sweet.

units.leftText: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom.
units.rightText: Who is wise and understanding among you? let him show by his good life his works in meekness of wisdom.

units.leftText: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, don’t boast and don’t lie against the truth.
units.rightText: But if ye have bitter jealousy and faction in your heart, glory not and lie not against the truth.

units.leftText: This wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic.
units.rightText: This wisdom is not a wisdom that cometh down from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.

units.leftText: For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed.
units.rightText: For where jealousy and faction are, there is confusion and every vile deed.

units.leftText: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
units.rightText: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, easy to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without variance, without hypocrisy.

units.leftText: Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.
units.rightText: And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace for them that make peace.

units.leftText: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?
units.rightText: Whence come wars and whence come fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your pleasures that war in your members?

units.leftText: You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. You fight and make war. You don’t have, because you don’t ask.
units.rightText: Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and covet, and cannot obtain: ye fight and war; ye have not, because ye ask not.

units.leftText: You ask, and don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.
units.rightText: Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may spend it in your pleasures.

units.leftText: You adulterers and adulteresses, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Whoever therefore wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.
units.rightText: Ye adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? Whosoever therefore would be a friend of the world maketh himself an enemy of God.

units.leftText: Or do you think that the Scripture says in vain, “The Spirit who lives in us yearns jealously”?
units.rightText: Or think ye that the scripture speaketh in vain? Doth the spirit which he made to dwell in us long unto envying?

units.leftText: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
units.rightText: But he giveth more grace. Wherefore the scripture saith, God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace to the humble.

units.leftText: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
units.rightText: Be subject therefore unto God; but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

units.leftText: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
units.rightText: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye doubleminded.

units.leftText: Lament, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom.
units.rightText: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness.

units.leftText: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.
units.rightText: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall exalt you.

units.leftText: Don’t speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother and judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
units.rightText: Speak not one against another, brethren. He that speaketh against a brother, or judgeth his brother, speaketh against the law, and judgeth the law: but if thou judgest the law, thou art not a doer of the law, but a judge.

units.leftText: Only one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge another?
units.rightText: One only is the lawgiver and judge, even he who is able to save and to destroy: but who art thou that judgest thy neighbor?

units.leftText: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow let’s go into this city and spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.”
units.rightText: Come now, ye that say, To-day or to-morrow we will go into this city, and spend a year there, and trade, and get gain:

units.leftText: Yet you don’t know what your life will be like tomorrow. For what is your life? For you are a vapor that appears for a little time and then vanishes away.
units.rightText: whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. What is your life? For ye are a vapor that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.

units.leftText: For you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.”
units.rightText: For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall both live, and do this or that.

units.leftText: But now you glory in your boasting. All such boasting is evil.
units.rightText: But now ye glory in your vauntings: all such glorying is evil.

units.leftText: To him therefore who knows to do good and doesn’t do it, to him it is sin.
units.rightText: To him therefore that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.

units.leftText: Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming on you.
units.rightText: Come now, ye rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming upon you.

units.leftText: Your riches are corrupted and your garments are moth-eaten.
units.rightText: Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are moth-eaten.

units.leftText: Your gold and your silver are corroded, and their corrosion will be for a testimony against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have laid up your treasure in the last days.
units.rightText: Your gold and your silver are rusted; and their rust shall be for a testimony against you, and shall eat your flesh as fire. Ye have laid up your treasure in the last days.

units.leftText: Behold, the wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you have kept back by fraud, cry out; and the cries of those who reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Armies.
units.rightText: Behold, the hire of the laborers who mowed your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth out: and the cries of them that reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.

units.leftText: You have lived in luxury on the earth, and taken your pleasure. You have nourished your hearts as in a day of slaughter.
units.rightText: Ye have lived delicately on the earth, and taken your pleasure; ye have nourished your hearts in a day of slaughter.

units.leftText: You have condemned and you have murdered the righteous one. He doesn’t resist you.
units.rightText: Ye have condemned, ye have killed the righteous one; he doth not resist you.

units.leftText: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receives the early and late rain.
units.rightText: Be patient therefore, brethren, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the husbandman waiteth for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receive the early and latter rain.

units.leftText: You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.
units.rightText: Be ye also patient; establish your hearts: for the coming of the Lord is at hand.

units.leftText: Don’t grumble, brothers, against one another, so that you won’t be judged. Behold, the judge stands at the door.
units.rightText: Murmur not, brethren, one against another, that ye be not judged: behold, the judge standeth before the doors.

units.leftText: Take, brothers, for an example of suffering and of perseverance, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
units.rightText: Take, brethren, for an example of suffering and of patience, the prophets who spake in the name of the Lord.

units.leftText: Behold, we call them blessed who endured. You have heard of the perseverance of Job and have seen the Lord in the outcome, and how the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
units.rightText: Behold, we call them blessed that endured: ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord, how that the Lord is full of pity, and merciful.

units.leftText: But above all things, my brothers, don’t swear—not by heaven, or by the earth, or by any other oath; but let your “yes” be “yes”, and your “no”, “no”, so that you don’t fall into hypocrisy.
units.rightText: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by the heaven, nor by the earth, nor by any other oath: but let your yea be yea, and your nay, nay; that ye fall not under judgment.
leftNotes: 5:12 TR reads “under judgment” instead of “into hypocrisy”

units.leftText: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.
units.rightText: Is any among you suffering? let him pray. Is any cheerful? let him sing praise.

units.leftText: Is any among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord;
units.rightText: Is any among you sick? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord:

units.leftText: and the prayer of faith will heal him who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.
units.rightText: and the prayer of faith shall save him that is sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, it shall be forgiven him.

units.leftText: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.
units.rightText: Confess therefore your sins one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The supplication of a righteous man availeth much in its working.

units.leftText: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it didn’t rain on the earth for three years and six months.
units.rightText: Elijah was a man of like passions with us, and he prayed fervently that it might not rain; and it rained not on the earth for three years and six months.

units.leftText: He prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit.
units.rightText: And he prayed again; and the heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.

units.leftText: Brothers, if any among you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back,
units.rightText: My brethren, if any among you err from the truth, and one convert him;

units.leftText: let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
units.rightText: let him know, that he who converteth a sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall cover a multitude of sins.
